verdict.rationale: Bento documents its own LLM-call tracing. It captures every span over OpenTelemetry, captures every LLM call at the SDK level, and offers `bento.track_ai` to wrap any LLM or tool call, with a span-tree view and cost per run. However, the evidence never says the traces record inputs, outputs, latency, or token counts; cost per run only hints at token usage. Missing for 10: documented capture of prompt inputs and model outputs, per-call latency/timing fields, explicit token-usage fields, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can capture traces of my LLM calls with inputs, outputs, latency, and token usage

citations.quote: Every span from every framework, captured over OpenTelemetry. Open the span tree, or follow a signal straight to the call that broke.
Wrap any LLM or tool call with bento.track_ai.
Bento captures every LLM call at the SDK level.
Capture every model call, tool call, and agent step from a Google ADK app with one line.
you see cost per run, tool failure rates, drift over prompt versions, and regressions across deploys out of the box.
